abstract: Constructing stable hyperholomorphic bundles with prescribed mixed Chern tensors is a remaining geometric step in attempts to represent exceptional Hodge classes on K3 powers. We prove a fusion theorem on a projective product $S\times Y$ with a selected K3 factor. Fix finitely many stable hyperholomorphic coefficients, independent of its tangent holonomy, with arbitrary finite multiplicities. At a point chosen generically after these coefficients, assume their restrictions admit a common hyperholomorphic bundle as both quotient and subbundle. Tensoring by a sufficiently large symmetric power of $T_S$ then yields a stable hyperholomorphic bundle with class $[A\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^lT_S]-[i_*U]$. Its normalized mixed second Chern character and its component with degree two in every factor are unchanged. Non-pseudoeffectivity of $T_S$ bounds the complete complementary restriction image; explicit high-weight vectors kill all source and supported Yoneda returns. We integrate the resulting perfect-object first jet using pure twistor weights and formality, and prove stability by restriction to a surface and the Uhlenbeck Bridgeland wall. We also determine the surviving high-spin restriction image at a prescribed point: torsion in the top direct image persists. This corrects an attempted application at a norm's own retraction point. Exact finite checks support the representation calculations. The common-restriction condition is realized by twists in one selected factor, but is not proved for the correlated determinant completion. No generic-power or mixed-product Hodge conjecture is claimed.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
title: Stable fusion at a generic K3 point with preservation of mixed Chern tensors
